sections.content:
# Tables

You can create tables with pipes `|` and hyphens `-`. Hyphens create each column's header, while pipes separate each column.

| First Header  | Second Header |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Content Cell  | Content Cell  |
| Content Cell  | Content Cell  |

## Alignment

You can align text to the left, right, or center of a column by including colons `:` to the left, right, or on both sides of the hyphens within the header row.

| Left-aligned | Center-aligned | Right-aligned |
| :---         |     :---:      |          ---: |
| git status   | git status     | git status    |
| git diff     | git diff       | git diff      |

## Formatting inside cells

You can use formatting such as links, inline code blocks, and text styling within your table. To include a pipe `|` as content within your cell, use a `\` before the pipe:

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `git status` | List all *new or modified* files |
| `git diff` | Show file differences that **haven't been** staged |
| `a \| b` | A cell with an escaped pipe |
| [Docs](https://docs.github.com) | A link in a cell |

# Collapsed sections

You can temporarily obscure sections of your Markdown by creating a collapsed section that the reader can choose to expand.

<details>

<summary>Tips for collapsed sections</summary>

### You can add a header

You can add text within a collapsed section.

You can add an image or a code block, too.

```ruby
   puts "Hello World"
```

</details>

## Open by default

To make the content appear open by default, add the `open` attribute to the `<details>` tag:

<details open>
<summary>Open by default</summary>

This section starts **expanded**. Markdown still works inside it when a blank line separates it from the tags.

- one
- two

</details>

## Nested collapsed sections

<details>
<summary>Outer</summary>

Outer text.

<details>
<summary>Inner</summary>

Inner text with `code`.

</details>

</details>

## Without blank lines

<details><summary>Tight markup</summary>
**This bold text** sits on the line after the summary, with no blank line.
</details>

# Code blocks

You can create fenced code blocks by placing triple backticks ` ``` ` before and after the code block.

```
function test() {
  console.log("notice the blank line before this function?");
}
```

    An indented code block,
    four spaces in.

## Syntax highlighting

You can add an optional language identifier to enable syntax highlighting in your fenced code block.

```ruby
require 'redcarpet'
markdown = Redcarpet.new("Hello World!")
puts markdown.to_html
```

```javascript
const greet = (name) => `Hello, ${name}`;
export default greet;
```

```json
{ "name": "renderizr", "private": true }
```

```diff
- const color = "colour";
+ const color = "color";
```

```shell
$ pnpm render workspace.json --single-file
```

```go
package main

func main() { println("hello") }
```

```dockerfile
FROM node:24-alpine
RUN corepack enable
```

```hcl
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "site" {
  bucket = "renderizr-site"
}
```

## Fences inside fences

To display triple backticks in a fenced code block, wrap them inside quadruple backticks.

````
```
Look! You can see my backticks.
```
````

~~~yaml
tildes: also fence
~~~

# Diagrams

You can create diagrams in Markdown using four different syntaxes: mermaid, geoJSON, topoJSON, and ASCII STL.

## Mermaid

```mermaid
graph TD;
    A-->B;
    A-->C;
    B-->D;
    C-->D;
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    Alice->>John: Hello John, how are you?
    John-->>Alice: Great!
```

## GeoJSON

```geojson
{
  "type": "Polygon",
  "coordinates": [
      [
          [-90,30],
          [-90,35],
          [-90,35],
          [-85,35],
          [-85,30]
      ]
  ]
}
```

## TopoJSON

```topojson
{
  "type": "Topology",
  "transform": {
    "scale": [0.0005000500050005, 0.00010001000100010001],
    "translate": [100, 0]
  },
  "objects": {
    "example": {
      "type": "GeometryCollection",
      "geometries": [
        {
          "type": "Point",
          "properties": {"prop0": "value0"},
          "coordinates": [4000, 5000]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "arcs": []
}
```

## STL

```stl
solid cube_corner
  facet normal 0.0 -1.0 0.0
    outer loop
      vertex 0.0 0.0 0.0
      vertex 1.0 0.0 0.0
      vertex 0.0 0.0 1.0
    endloop
  endfacet
  facet normal 0.0 0.0 -1.0
    outer loop
      vertex 0.0 0.0 0.0
      vertex 0.0 1.0 0.0
      vertex 1.0 0.0 0.0
    endloop
  endfacet
endsolid
```

# Mathematical expressions

To enable clear communication of mathematical expressions, GitHub supports LaTeX formatted math within Markdown.

## Inline expressions

To include a math expression inline with your text, delimit the expression with a dollar symbol `$`.

This sentence uses `$` delimiters to show math inline: $\sqrt{3x-1}+(1+x)^2$

To include a math expression inline with your text, delimit the expression with a dollar symbol and a backtick.

This sentence uses $\` and \`$ delimiters to show math inline: $`\sqrt{3x-1}+(1+x)^2`$

## Expressions as blocks

To add a math expression as a block, start a new line and delimit the expression with two dollar symbols `$$`.

**The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality**

$$\left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k b_k \right)^2 \leq \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k^2 \right) \left( \sum_{k=1}^n b_k^2 \right)$$

Alternatively, you can use the ` ```math ` code block syntax to display a math expression as a block.

**The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality**

```math
\left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k b_k \right)^2 \leq \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k^2 \right) \left( \sum_{k=1}^n b_k^2 \right)
```

## Dollar signs in and around expressions

To display a dollar sign as a character in the same line as a mathematical expression, you need to escape the non-delimiter `$`.

This expression uses `\$` to display a dollar sign: $`\sqrt{\$4}`$

To split \$100 in half, we calculate $100/2$

## Structurizr's syntax

Structurizr's documentation writes inline math as a code span wrapped in dollars: `$E = mc^2$`, and a block as a `katex` fence:

```katex
f(x) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty \hat f(\xi)\,e^{2 \pi i \xi x}\,d\xi
```

## Dollar signs that stay text

The license costs $5 a month, or $50 a year, and the upgrade runs $5-$10. A shell variable in code stays code: `echo $HOME and $PATH`.

```bash
echo "$HOME" && total=$((5 * 2))$
```

## Characters Markdown would otherwise read

Subscripts, stars and braces stay math: $a_1 * b_1 = a^* \cdot b_*$, $\{x \mid x > 0\}$, $a--b$ and $f'(x) = "y"$, while the prose around them keeps its "curly quotes" -- and dashes.

## A formula that fails to parse

The expression $\frac{1}{$ stays as written, and so does the block below.

```math
\left( x
```

## A long expression on a narrow screen

$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6} = 1 + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{36} + \frac{1}{49} + \frac{1}{64} + \frac{1}{81} + \cdots$$

# Autolinked references and URLs

## URLs

GitHub automatically creates links from standard URLs.

Visit https://github.com

Also www.github.com, a trailing period https://example.com/path. and an email address octocat@github.com.

Angle brackets always link: <https://structurizr.com>

## Issues and pull requests

Within conversations on GitHub, references to issues and pull requests are automatically converted to shortened links.

- Issue or pull request URL: https://github.com/jlord/sheetsee.js/issues/26
- `#` and issue or pull request number: #26
- `GH-` and issue or pull request number: GH-26
- `Username/Repository#` and issue or pull request number: jlord/sheetsee.js#26
- `Organization_name/Repository#` and issue or pull request number: github-linguist/linguist#4039

## Commit SHAs

- Commit URL: https://github.com/jlord/sheetsee.js/commit/a5c3785ed8d6a35868bc169f07e40e889087fd2e
- SHA: a5c3785ed8d6a35868bc169f07e40e889087fd2e
- `User@SHA`: jlord@a5c3785ed8d6a35868bc169f07e40e889087fd2e
- `Username/Repository@SHA`: jlord/sheetsee.js@a5c3785ed8d6a35868bc169f07e40e889087fd2e

## Mentions

Ping @octocat or the team @github/docs.

## Custom autolinks

A repository admin can link `JIRA-123` to an external tracker.

# Attached files GitHub uploads a file you drag into a comment and writes a link to it. An image becomes an image, a video plays in place, and any other file becomes a link. ## An image beside the document ![A diagram the workspace embeds](images/attached-diagram.svg) ## An uploaded image ![Screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a1d5d1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001) ## An uploaded video https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a1d5d1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000002 ## Another file [runbook.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/123456/runbook.pdf) ## Sizing with HTML

# Permalinks and keywords

## Permanent links to code

A permanent link to a specific line or range of lines in a file renders as a code snippet in issues and pull requests of the same repository.

https://github.com/octo-org/octo-repo/blob/9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b/README.md?plain=1#L14-L16

A permanent link to a Markdown file with `?plain=1`:

https://github.com/github/docs/blob/main/README.md?plain=1#L3

## Keywords in issues and pull requests

A pull request description that says these lines closes the issues when it merges:

Closes #10

Fixes octo-org/octo-repo#100

Resolves #10, resolves #123

# Footnotes

You can add footnotes to your content by using this bracket syntax:

Here is a simple footnote[^1].

A footnote can also have multiple lines[^2].

A footnote with a one-word definition[^word].

A named footnote[^note] keeps its number by order of reference.

[^1]: My reference.
[^2]: To add line breaks within a footnote, prefix new lines with 2 spaces.
  This is a second line.
[^word]: Single.
[^note]: Named footnotes still render with numbers, in the order they are referenced.

# Task lists

To create a task list, preface list items with a hyphen and space followed by `[ ]`. To mark a task as complete, use `[x]`.

- [x] #739
- [ ] https://github.com/octo-org/octo-repo/issues/740
- [ ] Add delight to the experience when all tasks are complete :tada:

If a task list item description begins with a parenthesis, you'll need to escape it with `\`:

- [ ] \(Optional) Open a followup issue

## Nested task lists

1. [ ] Write the spec
   - [x] Draft
   - [ ] Review
2. [X] Ship it

# Emoji

You can add emoji to your writing by typing `:EMOJICODE:`, a colon followed by the name of the emoji.

@octocat :+1: This PR looks great - it's ready to merge! :shipit:

Common shortcodes: :smile: :tada: :rocket: :warning: :white_check_mark: :x: :heart: :eyes:

GitHub's own custom emoji: :octocat: :shipit: :atom:

A Unicode emoji typed directly: 🚀 ✅

A time that looks like a shortcode: 10:30:45

# Images that follow the color scheme You can specify the theme an image is displayed for in Markdown by using the HTML `` element in combination with the `prefers-color-scheme` media feature. ## The picture element ## The picture element with embedded images The yellow image is the light one, the blue image the dark one. ## URL fragments The older way appends `#gh-dark-mode-only` or `#gh-light-mode-only` to the image URL. ![Light mode only](images/scheme-light.svg#gh-light-mode-only) ![Dark mode only](images/scheme-dark.svg#gh-dark-mode-only) ## URL fragments on embedded images The yellow image is the light one, the blue image the dark one. GitHub shows one of them. ![Light mode only](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAGAAAAAYCAIAAACKi2/DAAAASUlEQVR42u3YoREAIAwAsW6CwHQJ9h+AgcAhq4rL3U8Q+TFmqigQAGoCOnvpBQgQIECAAAECBAgQIECAAAECBAgQlxpInjSgD12HPiL3CVRrpQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==#gh-light-mode-only) ![Dark mode only](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAGAAAAAYCAIAAACKi2/DAAAASElEQVR42u3YoREAIAwAsVpGZeVOgUIhcMiq4nL3E0R+rH1UFAgANQGNmXoBAgQIECBAgAABAgQIECBAgAABAsSlBpInDehDF+cI6arSqqU4AAAAAElFTkSuQmCC#gh-dark-mode-only)

# HTML tags ## Keyboard keys Press Ctrl + Shift + P to open the command palette, or ⌘K on a Mac. ## Subscript and superscript This is a subscript text, and H2O is water. This is a superscript text, and E = mc2. ## Underline, insert and mark This text is underlined and this text is marked. ## Line breaks A line that ends with two spaces breaks here, one that ends with a backslash\ breaks here, and one that ends with a tag
breaks here too. ## Comments The comment above stays hidden. ## Attributes GitHub strips GitHub drops the style attribute, so this text shows in the body color there.

GitHub keeps align on a paragraph.

# Alerts

Alerts are a Markdown extension based on the blockquote syntax that you can use to emphasize critical information.

> [!NOTE]
> Useful information that users should know, even when skimming content.

> [!TIP]
> Helpful advice for doing things better or more easily.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Key information users need to know to achieve their goal.

> [!WARNING]
> Urgent info that needs immediate user attention to avoid problems.

> [!CAUTION]
> Advises about risks or negative outcomes of certain actions.

## Alerts with more inside

> [!NOTE]
> A first paragraph.
>
> A second paragraph with a list:
>
> - one
> - two

> [!tip]
> A lowercase marker.

> [!NOTE] Custom title
> GitHub renders text after the marker as a plain blockquote.

# Strikethrough

~~This was mistaken text~~ with two tildes.

~One tilde~ also strikes through on GitHub.

<del>The del tag</del> and <s>the s tag</s> strike through too.

# Split pages This section opens with an intro, then splits into pages at each `##` heading. A footnote referenced here[^intro] has its definition on the last page. ## First page The first page references a footnote[^first] and holds a collapsed section with a heading inside it.
A collapsed section with headings ## A page-level heading inside details Text under the page-level heading inside the collapsed section. ### A subheading inside details Text under the subheading.
Text after the collapsed section, still on the first page. ### A subheading on the first page The docs menu lists this subheading under the first page. ## Second page The second page references the same footnote again[^first] and one of its own[^second].
Tight details with a heading

An HTML heading inside details

Written in HTML.

## Third page The last page holds every footnote definition. It links back to [a subheading on the first page](#a-subheading-on-the-first-page) and to [the heading inside the collapsed section](#a-page-level-heading-inside-details). [^intro]: Defined at the end of the section, after the third page heading. [^first]: The first page's footnote, referenced twice. [^second]: The second page's footnote.

= AsciiDoc counterparts
:experimental:
:stem: latexmath

The AsciiDoc spelling of the same features, written as Asciidoctor's own documentation writes them.

== Tables

|git diff
|git diff

== Collapsible blocks

.Tips for collapsible blocks

====
You can add text within a collapsible block.

[source,ruby]
----

== Source blocks

    model {
        user = person "User"

== Math

Inline math: stem:[\sqrt{3x-1}+(1+x)^2] and latexmath:[E = mc^2].

[stem]
++++
\left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k b_k \right)^2 \leq \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k^2 \right)
++++

== Footnotes

A simple footnote.footnote:[My reference.] A named one.footnote:disclaimer[Named footnotes can repeat.] And again.footnote:disclaimer[]

== Checklists

* [*] checked
* [x] also checked
* [ ] not checked
* normal list item

== Keyboard keys

Press kbd:[Ctrl+Shift+P] to open the command palette, or kbd:[⌘ K] on a Mac. Choose menu:File[Save].

== Subscript and superscript

H~2~O is water, and E = mc^2^.

== Strikethrough

== Admonitions

decisions.title: Write the documentation in GitHub Flavored Markdown
decisions.content:
# 1. Write the documentation in GitHub Flavored Markdown

Date: 2026-11-13

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Authors read the documentation on GitHub first[^github], and they write it with the features GitHub renders.

| Feature | Where authors use it |
| --- | --- |
| Alerts | Every runbook |
| ~~Wiki pages~~ | Nowhere now |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The site must read the same as GitHub.

<details>
<summary>What GitHub renders</summary>

- [x] Tables
- [x] Alerts
- [ ] Math such as $E = mc^2$

</details>

## Decision

Write every section in GitHub Flavored Markdown. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd> to save, and keep H<sub>2</sub>O and x<sup>2</sup> readable. :rocket:

```mermaid
graph LR;
    Author-->GitHub;
    Author-->Renderizr;
```

```math
a^2 + b^2 = c^2
```

## Consequences

The site needs to render what GitHub renders. See https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github for the list.

[^github]: Most readers open a pull request before they open the site.

The cost of a lookup grows as $O(\log n)$ in the number of sections.
